correctness.rationale: For every d>=2, the imaginary-part identity proves that undamped modes are exactly the Hermitian eigenmodes vanishing at all d absorber vertices. The cyclic span of the target shell is the full (d-1)^2-dimensional standard-shell sector plus d+1 radial eigenmodes except one Krawtchouk middle mode precisely in even dimension. This is proved by explicit neighbor counts and Walsh eigenvectors, with no unproved nonstandard lemma. Orthogonal projection gives the formula for every site, and positivity of all individual rates guarantees decay on the complementary invariant sector even with defective nonnormal eigenvalues. Independent finite regression verified d=2..8 and 557 checks (max error <3.5e-12), but only the analytic derivation supports the infinite family.

value.rationale: Placing lossy detectors on the complete first Hamming shell is a canonical finite graph cut around an origin. The theorem answers the natural dark-space dimension and all initial-site absorption questions in closed form, reveals the counterintuitive odd/even perfect-absorption switch at the origin despite absorbing all its neighbors, and proves that the asymptotic outcome is robust to arbitrarily unequal positive loss strengths. These are exact structural diagnostics for quantum absorption; they are not mere recomputations of a small numerical table. The all-sites Krawtchouk correction resolves a nontrivial spectral degeneracy, and its meaning does not depend on an unproved downstream application.
